articles.title: A Leadership Crisis and the Call to Humility
articles.subtitle: Day 31: Sunday, 6 September 2026
articles.section: Expression of Humility in the Church
articles.content:
Psalm 139:23–24 (NIV)

Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts. See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

In the life of any church, moments of disagreement among leaders can test the very unity Christ prayed for. Some years ago, I found myself in such a season. After being entrusted with a senior leadership responsibility through a proper process, a group of fellow servants expressed deep concern and brought serious challenges against my continued service.

In that painful and pressured moment, the Lord gently but firmly reminded me that true leadership is not about defending position or reputation, but about reflecting the humility of Christ. Rather than reacting with frustration or control, I chose a path of restraint, openness, and trust in God’s processes and people.

This experience became a turning point in my understanding of humility — not as a weakness, but rather as a deliberate surrender to God’s ways for the sake of His church.

This week we will reflect on four expressions of humility that help leaders — and every believer — navigate conflict in a Christ-honouring way.
articles.reflection: Have you ever faced a moment when choosing humility preserved peace in your church or family?
prayers: Lord, search every heart in our churches. Remove pride and reveal where we need Your refining grace.
Pray that Malaysian church leaders will model Christlike humility in every disagreement, so the world may see our unity and believe.
Malaysia is known as a multi-racial, multi-religious nation that emphasises peace and harmony. Pray that the Government would uphold the Constitution that provides freedom for religious practices.

articles.title: Refusing to React — Allowing God to Search My Heart
articles.subtitle: Day 32: Monday, 7 September 2026
articles.section: Expression of Humility in the Church
articles.content:
Psalm 139:23–24 (NIV)

Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts. See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

When we face criticism or misunderstanding, especially from those we serve alongside, the first impulse is often to explain, correct, or defend ourselves immediately. Yet, humility invites us to pause.

In the season of conflict I experienced, I felt the Holy Spirit prompting me to hold back from quick replies. Instead, I quietly asked God to examine my own heart — to show me if any part of my attitude, decisions, or communication had contributed to the tension, even unintentionally.

This posture of inner stillness before God became a gift. It allowed Him to bring healing and clarity, even when the accusations themselves were not fully accurate. Humility begins when we let God search us first.
articles.reflection: Is there a situation today where God might be inviting you to pause and let Him examine your heart before you respond?
prayers: Father, quiet my heart when I feel attacked. Search me deeply and lead me in Your way of peace. Pray for leaders across Malaysia who are facing criticism — grant them grace to respond with humility rather than defensiveness.
Though all natural human desires have some legitimate, God-honouring purpose, they ought to be expressed appropriately in our lives. May our selfish motives not be a stumbling block to others.

Pray that harmony among all religious leaders would be expressed in respect and mutual understanding for each other’s practices. Only with these efforts can we attain unity through diversity as a nation.

articles.title: Welcoming Independent Scrutiny
articles.subtitle: Day 33: Tuesday, 8 September 2026
articles.section: Expression of Humility in the Church
articles.content:
Proverbs 15:22 (NIV)

Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.Humility is shown not only in private prayer, but in the willingness to be examined by others.

During that difficult season, I chose to invite an impartial group of respected servants to review the concerns raised against me. This meant stepping back from controlling the outcome and trusting that God could speak through the wider Body of Christ.

Such openness is never easy — it requires surrendering pride and the need to be proven right. Yet it declares clearly: “I belong to Christ’s church, and I trust His people to discern with me.” This act of humility often brings greater clarity and healing than any personal defence ever could.
articles.reflection: How willing are we, as individuals or as a church, to welcome wise and independent counsel when tensions arise?
prayers: Lord, give every leader courage to embrace accountability. Let us fear You more than we fear being misunderstood.
Pray that Malaysian churches will build cultures of healthy, transparent discernment that strengthen trust and unity.

As Christians, we continue to pray for the Unity Government to embrace integrity, transparency, accountability and justice. Irrespective how the Government came into being, we affirm that the authority that exists has been instituted by God.

articles.title: Submitting to Church Process and Governance
articles.subtitle: Day 34: Wednesday, 9 September 2026
articles.section: Expression of Humility in the Church
articles.content:
Hebrews 13:17a (NIV)

Have confidence in your leaders and submit to their authority, because they keep watch over you as those who must give an account.

Humility reaches its fullest expression when we honour the structures God has placed in His church, even when they feel costly.

In the conflict I faced, I willingly placed the matter before the wider assembly and its established processes. This choice meant accepting that the final decision might not go the way I hoped — yet it also affirmed that Christ alone is Head of the church, and no single leader stands above His Body.

Submitting to godly processes guards against division, prevents personal agendas from taking over, and testifies to the watching world that we truly belong to one another under Christ.
articles.reflection: Where might pride be resisting proper church processes in your life or fellowship? How can humble submission bring healing?
prayers: Lord Jesus, teach us to honour the processes You have given Your church, even when they test our hearts.
Pray for unity and mutual submission among Malaysian believers — that every local church and denomination may reflect the humility and harmony of Christ.
Pray for the religious leaders representing interfaith groups - that all would be people who uphold integrity, not leading carelessly in moral compromise.

articles.title: Acknowledging Our Poverty
articles.subtitle: Day 35: Thursday, 10 September 2026
articles.section: Expression of Humility in the Church
articles.content:
Matthew 5:3 (NIV)

“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”

The Bible describes humility as meekness, lowliness, and absence of self. The Greek word translated to “humility” in Colossians 3:12 and elsewhere literally means “lowliness of mind.” So, we see that humility is a heart attitude, not merely an outward demeanour. One may put on an outward show of humility but still have a heart full of pride and arrogance. Jesus said that those who are “poor in spirit” would have the kingdom of heaven (see Matthew 5:3). Being poor in spirit means that only those who admit to an absolute bankruptcy of spiritual worth will inherit eternal life. Therefore, humility is essential for the Christian.

When we come to Christ as sinners, we must come in humility. We acknowledge that we are paupers and beggars who come with nothing to offer Him but our sin and our need for salvation. We recognise our lack of merit and our complete inability to save ourselves. Then when He offers the grace and mercy of God, we accept it in humble gratitude and commit our lives to Him and to others. We “die to self” so that we can live as new creations in Christ (see 2 Corinthians 5:17). We never forget that He has exchanged our worthlessness for His infinite worth, and our sin for His righteousness. The life we now live, we live by faith in the Son of God who loved us and gave Himself for us (see Galatians 2:20). That is true humility.
prayers: Pray that we would serve Him with a humble heart and prioritise God in whatever we do.

Through humility there is deep fellowship (kononia) that permeates us to share things in common. Pray that the Church, as a community, would worship God in total humility, trusting Him who directs our paths.
A nation close to 70 years of Merdeka (independence) has developed some measure of unity. Pray that we will share our resources with those who are less fortunate or marginalised

articles.title: Submission to God’s Calling
articles.subtitle: Day 36: Friday, 11 September 2026
articles.section: Expression of Humility in the Church
articles.content:
2 Chronicles 7:14 (NIV)

“If My people… humble themselves and pray… then I will hear from heaven…”

The world around us is experiencing upheaval in every sphere—political, social, economic, and religious. As the Church, we affirm our faith that God is able to bring transformation to all circumstances. All Christians are called to approach God with an attitude of humility. The humility of God’s people invites His divine intervention.

The calling of the Church is to humble ourselves collectively and to kneel before God as an expression of complete surrender. Through corporate prayer, the Church acknowledges its total dependence upon God, not upon human strength. This submission is a beautiful picture of Christ’s relationship with God the Father, and sets a wonderful example for the Church to follow.

When the people of God unite in humility, God works to restore and guide the direction of the Church.

“If My people… humble themselves and pray… then I will hear from heaven…” (2 Chronicles 7:14, NIV).

God exalts the humble (James 4:10).
prayers: Pray that the local church would grow and experience the pouring presence of the Holy Spirit.

Remember the Highly Priestly Prayer in John 17:21 that the local church will experience the oneness and the presence of the Holy Spirit and be united as one body in Christ? Pray for this unity in the Church.

The general behaviour of a nation’s citizen speaks volumes of the integrity and wellbeing of its people. Since 2026 is Visit Malaysia Year, let us work together to make the slogan - Malaysia, Truly Asia - a memorable experience for our visitors.

articles.title: Humility to God’s Sovereignty through the Church
articles.subtitle: Day 37: Saturday, 12 September 2026
articles.section: Expression of Humility in the Church
articles.content:
Read Philippians 2:5 - 8

The Church is the body of Christ and is the expression of Christ to the world, established because the Lord Jesus was willing to humble Himself and set aside His heavenly glory as the Son of God. Philippians 2 tells us that “Christ Jesus who, being in the form of God, made Himself of no reputation, taking the form of a bond servant, and coming in the likeness of men. And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to the point of death, even death on the cross” (v. 5-8, NKJV).

Christ’s humility and obedience formed the foundation of His church, which He expects to be demonstrated to the world. God’s people are reminded to “have the same mind as Christ, doing nothing through selfish ambition or conceit. Instead, in lowliness of mind, they are to esteem others better than themselves” (Philippians 2:3, NKJV).

In the New Testament, the Lord’s calling to His people is clear: they are to live as disciples and servants (Luke 14:26-27; Mark 10:43-45). The Lord said, “Yet it shall not be so among you; but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant. And whoever of you desires to be first shall be slave of all. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many” (Mark 10:43-45, NKJV).

Servanthood is the mark of humility and portrays the very character and nature of our Lord Jesus Himself. This is the Lord’s primary calling to His church - to become more like Him in love, compassion and humility. As His people, our maturity is measured by how closely we reflect His character and servant heart to the world.
prayers: Pray that we are transformed in our inner man, gaining the heart and compassion of a servant to serve others. Pray for boldness and passion to testify and share Christ with the world.

Each of us differs in our own journey of drawing close to God, therefore there should not be any comparison. Pray that we will align to His will, so that we will arrive at the destiny that the Lord intended for each of us.

For the sake of good democratic governance in Malaysia, pray for opposition parties that monitor the government of the day for purposes of accountability and compliance with the constitution and laws of the nation.

articles.title: Walking Humbly with Our God
articles.subtitle: Day 38: Sunday, 13 September 2026
articles.content:
Closing Summary for the 40 Days of Fasting & Prayer

Micah 6:8

“He has told you, O man, what is good… to walk humbly with your God?”

As we review our journey over 40 days of fasting and prayer, we pause to acknowledge what the Lord has been forming within us. This journey was never meant to end with the fast itself; rather, it was intended to shape a lifelong posture of humility before God. Micah 6:8 remains our enduring call — moving beyond religious activity to a daily walk that reflects justice, mercy, and humility.

Fasting has quietened our appetites and recalibrated our hearts, reminding us that true humility is not weakness, but strength expressed through dependence on God. Scripture assures us, “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble” (James 4:6). The true measure of success these days is not what we abstain from; but how our hearts have been aligned to know Him (Daniel 11:32b) and find the strength to resist daily temptations (Deut. 8:3). God intentionally led the Israelites through hunger to reveal that physical provision isn’t enough. He showed them - and us - that it is His Word that gives us the true strength to face and overcome our daily temptations. His Word keeps our spiritual quotient (SQ) steady and anchored above our physical, mental, and emotional fluctuations. Therefore, the daily, disciplined reading of Scripture must be our daily priority. A simple reminder: NBNB (No Bible, No Breakfast) and NSNS (No Scripture, No Sleep).

Jesus Christ stands as our perfect example. Though He was fully God, “he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death - even death on a cross.” (Philippians 2:6–8). As followers of Christ, we are invited to carry His humility in our decisions, our service, and our relationships. Jesus Himself calls us to “learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart” (Matthew 11:29).

As the fast concludes, let humility continue. Let God’s Word remain our daily anchor, guarding us from pride and keeping our steps aligned with His truth (Deut. 17:19–20). May the lessons learned in these 40 days shape the days ahead, producing obedience, unity, and quiet faithfulness.
prayers: Lord, we humble ourselves before You. Thank You for meeting us in this sacred season. Form in us a heart like Christ’s — obedient, surrendered, and faithful. As we move forward, may we walk humbly with You, serving others and glorifying Your name in all we do. Amen.

articles.title: The Lasting Reward of Humility
articles.subtitle: Day 39: Monday, 14 September 2026
articles.content:
Closing Devotional for the 40 Days’ Journey

Read Jeremiah 9:23–24 | 1 John 2:15–16

As we come to the close of these 40 Days of Fasting and Prayer, the Lord gently recenters our hearts on what truly matters. “Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, let not the mighty man boast in his might… but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me…” (Jer. 9:23–24). Humility turns our focus away from our own achievements and redirects it toward the greatest reward of all — knowing the Lord and delighting in His ways.

The fruit of humility is intimacy with God. When we set aside our pride, our hearts become soft, teachable, and responsive to His voice. However, Scripture also warns us of daily hindrances that wear down humility. “The desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes, and pride of life…” (1 John 2:15–16) continually compete for our affection. These subtle pressures draw us toward self-reliance, comparison, and misplaced confidence, slowly shifting our trust away from God.

This is why humility must be intentionally guarded. It is not sustained by fasting or spiritual experiences alone, but by a steady, faithful devotion to God’s Word. When human affirmation fades and our strength feels limited, the Lord remains faithful. Paul’s testimony reminds us, “At my first defense no one came to stand by me… But the Lord stood by me…” (2 Tim. 4:16–17). God’s presence and truth anchor us when circumstances and people let us down. Let us continue to feed our soul with the Word as our daily discipline. In humility, we find clarity for our steps, the strength to keep going, and deep joy of knowing the Lord.

One Practical Step

Set aside a fixed daily time to read and meditate on God’s Word, allowing Scripture to shape your heart before the demands of the day.
prayers: Lord, we choose to boast only in knowing You. Guard our hearts from worldly desires and the pride of life. Root us deeply in Your Word, and keep us humble, faithful, and steadfast. Form in us a teachable spirit — strong enough to repent, gentle enough to say, “I am sorry that I’ve offended you,” and willing to walk in reconciliation and peace. Let our lives reflect the fruit of the Holy Spirit and bring glory to Your name. As Your Word declares, “The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet” (Romans 16:20). May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with us always. Amen.
